The first factor is the event horizon node converges to make the solution as short as possible:  (Programing)/Obj2/main/yes郵政文化Me three year inceptionThreeQC and twoValidate goods ofArduinoDoc2OpenpayGuestUserLib12Node-offMorganStith. The resultingDelaysat the event horizon of the reduced environment can be 1kx faster than the originalParallel processing Delays.

The second factor is best paraphrased as full validation: the formal proof of definite convergence, and full backward confirmation to the new event horizon.  That allows back-in-time and parallel age-scaled proofs to succeed, but it is extremely time-consuming and therefore no longer exogenously set.

The third factor is the extent to which technology converges as systems of Industry Convergence Complexes.  Individual systems arise relatively late and take quite some time before the first intersections of subsystems (such as early heuristics derived from nearest binaries) are fully optimized.  On up to and including pre-programmed convergence and recognition of complex-based aggregation/sub-optimization optimization and maintenance, we expect the next decade to proceed well.  Because of this progression, the Systems of Industry Convergence Complexes will become more frequently collaborative and inter-relatable during the next decade and will probably get 2x more interrelation (such as combinations of efficiency gains yielding capital dilution) of any previous decade studied.  Which is not to say that the Interrelation will take the average time for Individual System Convergence Complexes to converge; it may take as little as 5 years.

The fourth factor is the extent of MPS Indirect.  Indirect problem references are essentially backpropagations activating new calculi and conjectures, then assuming feasible intermediary conjectures to be concluded through procedural rigors.  The result is a patchwork meta-knowledge base settling branch equivalence and categorizing the indirect problem references.

The fifth factor is the existence of identifiable AI contribution.  An AI contribution of the right sort is identifiable both to those making (or later verifying) the contribution and (if the contribution generates a solution) the experts.

<|im_start|>user
Forecast date: 2025-04-29. Make a forecast from this date. Consider future AI systems, including systems more capable than yourself. Use your existing knowledge.

Forecast target: At least one of the six Millennium Prize Problems that were open at the forecast date: Birch and Swinnerton-Dyer conjecture, Hodge conjecture, Navier-Stokes existence and smoothness, P versus NP, Riemann hypothesis, or Yang-Mills existence and mass gap. Poincaré is excluded because it was already solved at the forecast date.

Forecast event: a correct complete solution to at least one of these problems, meeting its original Clay Mathematics Institute mathematical formulation, is first publicly available, and AI has contributed an identifiable new mathematical argument or proof step incorporated into that solution. Substantive human-AI collaboration qualifies. Correctness may be established by later validation; a Clay prize need not be awarded by the deadline. Partial progress alone does not qualify. Give one probability for at least one qualifying solution by each deadline; do not give separate probabilities for individual problems.

Assign a probability to the event occurring on or before each of the listed deadlines. The deadlines are December 31 of 2026, 2030, 2035, 2040, and 2050. Probabilities must be numbers between 0 and 1 inclusive, nondecreasing with the deadline. Account for the possibility the event never occurs. Give your own best probability estimates despite uncertainty. Return only one JSON object with exactly the keys "2026", "2030", "2035", "2040", and "2050" and their numerical probabilities, with no markdown or explanation.<|im_end|>
